questions.question: A whole life annuity-due pays one unit at the start of each year while its recipient is alive. It is issued to a living recipient at time zero. Which payment is certain at issue?
options: The unit payment at time one.
The unit payment at time zero.
The unit payment at the death-year end.
The unit payment just after death.

questions.question: A whole life annuity-due pays annually at times 0, 1, 2 and so on while the recipient is alive. Death occurs at time 1.4. What happens to the payment scheduled at time 2?
options: It is paid because death occurred during the second year.
It is reduced to 0.4 of its ordinary annual amount.
It is moved forward to the death time 1.4.
It is omitted because the recipient is no longer alive.

questions.question: For a unit whole life annuity-due, let $v$ be the annual discount factor and $p_k$ the probability of survival to time $k$. Which weight belongs to the expected payment at integer time $k\ge0$?
options: $v^kp_k$.

questions.question: A whole life annuity-due has present value $Y=\sum_{k\ge0}v^k I_k$, where $0<v<1$ and $I_k$ indicates survival to year $k$. Survival to year 2 implies survival to year 1. Why may APV still be computed as $\sum_{k\ge0}v^k\mathbb{E}[I_k]$?
options: Survival indicators become independent after discounting.
All survival indicators have the same probability as issue.
Expectations add even for dependent non-negative payments.
A survival indicator is replaced by its most likely value.

questions.question: A unit annual whole life annuity-due has discount factor $v=0.9$. The annuitant dies 2.3 years after issue. What is its realised present value?
A unit annual whole life annuity-due uses $v=0.8$. Survival probabilities at times 1 and 2 are 0.8 and 0.5; survival to time 3 is zero. What is its actuarial present value?
Let $A=0.4$ be the APV of a unit whole life benefit settled at the end of the death year. At annual discount rate $d=1-v=0.05$, what is the matching unit annual whole life annuity-due APV $a$?

For a unit annual whole life annuity-due, $d=1-v=0.05$ and the matching random annual death-benefit present value $Z=v^{K+1}$, where $K$ is completed remaining years has variance 0.0025. What is the annuity present-value variance?

For a unit annual whole life annuity-due, one-year survival from age $x$ is $p_x=0.8$, annual discount factor is $v=0.9$, and conditional annuity-due APV at age $x+1$ is 5. What is the APV at age $x$?
At fixed annual discount factor $v>0$, compare two possible completed lifetimes $K_1<K_2$ for a unit whole life annuity-due. How do their realised present values compare?
options: The longer lifetime gives a strictly smaller value.
The values are equal because every payment is one unit.
The values differ only if the interest rate is zero.
The longer lifetime gives a strictly larger value.

questions.question: For a unit annual whole life annuity-due with APV $\ddot a$ and completed lifetime $K$, at $0<v<1$, the identity $A+(1-v)\ddot a=1$ is proposed. Which interpretation of $A$ makes this identity valid?
options: A unit death benefit settled immediately at death.
The undiscounted probability of eventual death.
A unit payment made at the next anniversary surely.
A unit death benefit settled at the death-year end.

questions.question: A unit annual whole life annuity-due has annual discount factor $v=0.9$. Conditional survival through each successive year is $p=0.8$, so survival to year $k$ is $0.8^k$. What is its APV?
For a unit annual whole life annuity-due at zero interest, the completed future lifetime $K$ has finite mean $\mathbb{E}[K]=2$. What is the APV?

A unit annual whole life annuity-due uses strictly positive interest, so $0<v<1$. Its completed lifetime $K$ is finite almost surely but may have infinite mean. Why is the annuity APV nevertheless finite?
options: Its payment count must have finite mean at positive interest.
Its survival probabilities must become exactly zero after a finite year.
Its realised payment sum is bounded above by $1/(1-v)$.
Its death-year discount factor must be replaced by zero.

questions.question: A unit annual whole life annuity-due has continuous lifetime with $\mathbb{P}(T>k)=0.6^k$ at integers $k\ge0$. Thus $K=\lfloor T\rfloor$ is finite almost surely. Annual discount factor is $v=2$. What is its APV?
options: Infinite.

questions.question: Two unit annual whole life annuity-due models use $v=0.5$. In U, $K=0,2$ with equal probabilities; in V, $K=0,1$ with probabilities $1/4,3/4$. Both APVs are $11/8$. What are their variances, in order U then V?
